docs.title: lua-slds · v0.2
docs.text:
SLDS = Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics. This pure Lua library defines short link behavior independently of HTTP, database clients, caches and authorization. Core has zero runtime dependencies and supports Lua 5.1, Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT.

SLDS 只定义短链是什么、如何变更以及何时可以解析。宿主显式组装依赖；四个用例由 Interactor 编排，Core 只使用 Repository 与可选 CodeGenerator 两个端口。Generator/Encoder 是 Adapter 内部组件。

docs.title: Start with an explicit code
docs.text:
These examples target the v0.2 source API. Install the current checkout with luarocks make lua-slds-scm-1.rockspec:

local slds = require("slds")
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
})
local link = assert(interactor:create({}, {
    code = "hello", target = "https://example.com/long/path",
}))
local result = assert(interactor:resolve({}, slds.Identity.new(link.namespace, link.code)))
if result.resolvable then print(result.target) end

docs.title: Behavioral boundaries
docs.text:
• Identity is a logically immutable { namespace, code } tuple.
  • Lifecycle stores ACTIVE, DISABLED or terminal DELETED; expires_at <= now derives EXPIRED during resolution.
  • Resolve reports both existence (found) and permission to resolve (resolvable); errors remain separate.
  • Writes apply sparse patches against the latest authoritative state. Deleted identities remain reserved.
  • Metadata and Hook payloads use independent raw-table snapshots. ctx stays shared and should be read-only.
  • Hooks execute synchronously; callback errors are isolated, callback latency is not.
  • Core does not provide caches, external concurrency coordination, HTTP routing, analytics delivery or authorization.

v0.2 changes public names and Hook signatures. Read the migration guide before updating an integration.

docs.title: Root module
docs.text:
require("slds") exports:

Field Value / module slds.VERSION "0.2.0" slds.new Factory equivalent to Interactor.new slds.Interactor slds.interactor slds.Identity slds.domain.identity slds.ShortLink slds.domain.short_link slds.Lifecycle slds.domain.lifecycle slds.Resolution slds.domain.resolution slds.Errors slds.domain.errors slds.Hooks slds.hooks slds.HookPoint slds.hook_point

There are no flat status/error aliases, Service, or adapter exports. Require adapters explicitly. Factories use dot notation; instance methods use colon notation.

docs.title: slds.new(opts) -> Interactor
docs.text:
Option Required Contract repository yes Table with create/get/update/delete methods code_generator no Table with generate(ctx,input); returns final Code lifecycle no Partial table of is_valid/can_transition/is_resolvable functions clock no Function returning a finite number; defaults to os.time hooks no Hooks-compatible table with on/before/after; defaults to empty Hooks

Construction checks method types and fills missing Lifecycle predicates with defaults without mutating the host's table. Supply the same effective Lifecycle functions to the authoritative Repository. ctx must be a table; Core passes the same reference through, without interpreting it.

docs.title: interactor:create(ctx,input) -> ShortLink | nil,err
docs.text:
Input field Contract namespace Non-empty string; defaults to "default" only when nil code Optional non-empty string; only nil invokes CodeGenerator target Non-empty string; rejects javascript:, data: and file: schemes after whitespace/case normalization expires_at Optional finite number metadata Optional opaque table, captured as an independent raw-table graph status Must be omitted; Interactor creates ACTIVE

Core does not fetch or fully parse target URLs. Host URL policy may be stricter. Empty/wrong-type Code returns INVALID without generation. Missing Code without CodeGenerator returns INVALID. Generation receives the original ctx and an independent input snapshot. Generated Code must be a non-empty string; Core does not coerce or retry. Repository enforces uniqueness, including deleted identities.

docs.title: interactor:resolve(ctx,identity) -> ResolutionResult | nil,err
docs.text: Captures identity, reads Repository once, then applies Resolution and the injected clock. Repository NOT_FOUND becomes a normal result with found=false,resolvable=false,status=NOT_FOUND; infrastructure errors remain nil,err. Resolution never writes storage.

docs.title: interactor:update(ctx,identity,patch) -> ShortLink | nil,err
docs.text:
Captures identity/patch and calls Repository.update directly, without a preliminary get. Only target/status/expires_at are allowed. Unknown keys, including metadata, return INVALID. Namespace/code patches raise a programming error. Missing record returns NOT_FOUND; terminal records, invalid fields, rejected rules or can_update return INVALID. Unspecified fields remain unchanged.

expires_at=nil means no change. No clearing sentinel is defined; false returns INVALID.

docs.title: interactor:delete(ctx,identity) -> true | nil,err
docs.text: Calls Repository.delete without a preliminary get. Logical deletion validates the latest record, target state and transition, then retains the identity. Repeat deletion returns INVALID; missing identity returns NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: interactor:use(hook) -> Interactor
docs.text:
Convenience registration into the same Hooks registry. hook maps HookPoint values to functions; invalid keys/callbacks raise a programming error. It is chainable and uses only v0.2 signatures:

interactor:use({
    [slds.HookPoint.AFTER_CREATE] = function(ctx, point, link, err)
        if link then print(point, link.code) else print(point, err) end
    end,
})

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
Identity.new(namespace,code) requires two non-empty strings. Identity.new(code) uses Identity.DEFAULT_NAMESPACE, "default". Shared metatable methods provide value equality and tostring(identity) as namespace:code.

Identity is an ordinary table with logical immutability: callers must not rewrite fields. The string representation is for display; it is not a collision-free storage key. Store the tuple unambiguously, including strings containing NUL.

docs.title: ShortLink
docs.text:
ShortLink.new(data,lifecycle?) -> ShortLink | nil,INVALID accepts namespace/code, target, optional status (defaults ACTIVE), expires_at and metadata. Invalid/missing identity fields or a non-table container are programming errors; invalid target/status/expiration/metadata returns INVALID.

link:with_patch(patch,lifecycle?) -> ShortLink | nil,INVALID creates a new validated entity. Only explicit target/status/expires_at fields are applied; unknown keys are rejected, immutable keys raise an error, and DELETED cannot be updated. Same-status patches do not invoke the transition predicate.

link:is_expired(now) -> boolean requires finite now and compares expires_at <= now.

link:to_table() -> table exports plain data with independent metadata. Construction, patch and export copy raw table graphs, retaining cycles/shared children and table keys without transporting or invoking metadata metatables. Non-table leaves retain their original values; host resource internals are not isolated. There is no ShortLink:is_resolvable method; use Resolution.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Member Meaning ACTIVE / DISABLED / DELETED The only persistent statuses is_valid(status) Default accepts those three statuses can_transition(from,to) Default permits ACTIVE↔DISABLED and ACTIVE/DISABLED→DELETED is_resolvable(status) Default true only for ACTIVE

A partial override provides only the predicates being changed; each must be a pure synchronous function. Rules may restrict allowed states/transitions. Custom resolvability may permit DISABLED, but DELETED is never resolvable and expired records remain denied. Unknown persistent statuses and terminal revival cannot be authorized by an override. No STATUSES array or validate_transition helper is exported.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution.resolve(link,identity,now,lifecycle?) -> ResolutionResult evaluates, in order: absence → DELETED → lifecycle denial → expiration → success. Resolution.not_found(identity) constructs absence; Resolution.not_resolvable(link,status) and Resolution.resolvable(link) construct result snapshots. The latter helpers construct results only; callers wanting decisions must use resolve.

Field Contract found Whether the identity exists resolvable Whether the host may resolve it now namespace, code Identity target Present only when resolvable status Actual lifecycle status, Resolution.EXPIRED, or Errors.NOT_FOUND expires_at Stored optional expiration

Custom rules permitting DISABLED resolution preserve DISABLED in the result. Expiration is derived at expires_at <= now, never persisted. ResolutionResult is independent of the entity and has the shared Resolution metatable.

docs.title: Errors and dependency responses
docs.text:
Error Expected use Errors.NOT_FOUND Missing Repository identity Errors.CONFLICT Duplicate create or adapter-declared conditional commit conflict Errors.INVALID Invalid business fields, transitions, terminal writes or policy rejection

Expected failures return nil,err, without added prefixes. Infrastructure errors retain their original values. Success returns result,nil; delete success must be true. Dependency nil,nil, result plus non-nil error, wrong record type or wrong delete success type is a programming error. Unexpected exceptions propagate. Programming errors are not guaranteed AFTER callbacks.

docs.title: Hooks and HookPoint
docs.text:
Hooks.new() creates an empty registry. hooks:on(point,fn) appends a callback and returns the registry. Points are BEFORE, AFTER, BEFORE_CREATE/AFTER_CREATE, BEFORE_RESOLVE/AFTER_RESOLVE, BEFORE_UPDATE/AFTER_UPDATE, BEFORE_DELETE/AFTER_DELETE and ON_ERROR. Their values are lower-case strings such as "before_create".

Order: general BEFORE → specific BEFORE → operation → specific AFTER → general AFTER. Each point preserves registration order. BEFORE follows argument-container/identity checks and input capture, preceding generation and business validation. Every normal return, including INVALID/CONFLICT and infrastructure errors, reaches AFTER.

Point Callback BEFORE_CREATE fn(ctx,point,input) BEFORE_RESOLVE / BEFORE_DELETE fn(ctx,point,identity) BEFORE_UPDATE fn(ctx,point,identity,patch) AFTER_CREATE / AFTER_UPDATE fn(ctx,point,link,err) AFTER_RESOLVE fn(ctx,point,result,err) AFTER_DELETE fn(ctx,point,ok,err) ON_ERROR fn(ctx,failed_point,hook_err)

General observers receive the actual operation point and corresponding arguments. ON_ERROR's second argument is the failed point; its own exceptions are isolated without recursion. Each callback gets independent domain payload snapshots, preserved root domain methods and nil argument positions. ctx is shared, read-only by convention. Callback returns are ignored; pcall isolates exceptions, not latency, mutation of ctx or event durability.

Dispatcher methods hooks:before(ctx,specific_before_point,...) and hooks:after(ctx,specific_after_point,...) reject incorrect points. Hosts normally register observers and let Interactor dispatch.

docs.title: Core ports
docs.text:
require("slds.ports.repository") and require("slds.ports.code_generator") document interfaces; their stub methods raise errors. Implementations use duck typing, with no inheritance requirement.

Method Success / failure repository:create(ctx,link) Independent ShortLink / nil,err; atomic identity uniqueness repository:get(ctx,identity) Independent ShortLink / nil,NOT_FOUND or infrastructure error repository:update(ctx,identity,patch) Updated independent ShortLink / nil,err; latest-state atomic validation/commit repository:delete(ctx,identity) true / nil,err; terminal logical deletion code_generator:generate(ctx,input) Final non-empty string / nil,err

Repository updates validate a complete candidate using the raw sparse patch before calling an optional can_update(current,patch). This authoritative pure, synchronous, non-yielding boolean predicate is injected only into the Repository. False returns INVALID; exception or non-boolean is a programming error and must leave storage unchanged. Its arguments must not affect committed data if mutated. Delete uses the same full entity/transition validation, without calling can_update. Atomicity must be implemented by the actual storage adapter, not by a Core pre-read.

docs.title: Bundled adapters
docs.text:
Module / constructor Scope slds.adapters.inmemory.repository.new({lifecycle?,can_update?}) Nested namespace/code map; independent snapshots; atomic non-yielding methods within one Lua VM slds.adapters.composed.code_generator.new({generator,encoders?}) Inner generate(ctx), then ordered encoder:encode(previous); final Code validation slds.adapters.sequential.generator.new(start?) Exact integer start in [0,9007199254740991], default 1 only for nil; uniqueness only within that instance slds.adapters.base62.encoder.new() Pure deterministic alphabet 0–9,A–Z,a–z; exact integers in [0,9007199254740991]

Composed captures a dense encoder array at construction; holes/non-encoder entries are programming errors. Empty arrays are valid when the inner generator already returns Code. Intermediate values are opaque; only nil means failure. First failure stops the pipeline and passes its error unchanged. Nil,nil or value+error is a programming error. Final empty/non-string output returns INVALID. The input argument is unused by this reference adapter.

Sequential returns the maximum once, then persistently returns nil,"generator exhausted". Invalid starts or unsupported Base62 inputs raise errors. Base62's range does not support full uint64; do not use tonumber to coerce large string IDs. External generators/encoders must agree on representation and range; Repository remains the uniqueness authority. No external Redis/Postgres/cache adapter is bundled.

docs.title: Supply a direct CodeGenerator
docs.text:
Implement one method returning final Code. Use this when the host already has its own identifier service or code algorithm:

local generator = {
    generate = function(self, ctx, input)
        return "campaign-" .. input.metadata.campaign
    end,
}
local slds = require("slds")
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
    code_generator = generator,
})
local link = assert(interactor:create({}, {
    target = "https://example.com", metadata = { campaign = "spring" },
}))

The example intentionally produces a deterministic Code: repeated creation conflicts, rather than becoming an idempotency API. Repository enforces uniqueness. Core passes unchanged ctx and an independent input snapshot. Return nil,err for expected failures; nil,nil is a programming error. Core performs no automatic retry or numeric coercion.

For internal Generator/Encoder composition, use the bundled Composed adapter. Its encoder array is dense and ordered; an empty array is valid if the inner generator already returns Code. The current Base62 accepts only exact integers in [0,2^53-1]; full uint64/string identifiers need a compatible external encoder. Do not coerce them with tonumber.

docs.title: Customize Lifecycle and authoritative update policy
docs.text:
Supply the same rules to Interactor and Repository. Missing predicates use defaults; the original table is not modified:

local slds = require("slds")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository")
local rules = {
    can_transition = function(from, to)
        return slds.Lifecycle.can_transition(from, to)
            and not (from == slds.Lifecycle.DISABLED and to == slds.Lifecycle.ACTIVE)
    end,
}
local repo = Repository.new({
    lifecycle = rules,
    can_update = function(current, patch)
        return patch.target == nil or patch.target == current.target
    end,
})
local interactor = slds.new({ repository = repo, lifecycle = rules })

This example prevents re-enabling a disabled link and prevents changing target. Invalid field values are rejected before can_update executes. The predicate receives the latest entity and raw sparse patch; false returns INVALID, while a thrown error or non-boolean is a programming error. It must be pure, synchronous and non-yielding. It does not run for delete. Its mutation cannot become committed data.

No override can admit an unknown persistent status, revive DELETED, resolve DELETED or bypass expiration. A custom is_resolvable may allow DISABLED, in which case the result retains status DISABLED. The host should use result.resolvable.

docs.title: Implement an authoritative Repository
docs.text:
Provide create/get/update/delete; see exact signatures. No inheritance is needed. On success return an independent ShortLink, except delete returns true. Missing identity returns nil,Errors.NOT_FOUND, never nil,nil. Pass infrastructure errors unchanged.

For update, perform the following inside the adapter's atomic commit mechanism:

  1. Read the latest record and reject missing/DELETED state.
  2. Build a complete candidate using current:with_patch(patch,lifecycle), validating fields, allowed keys and transitions.
  3. Evaluate optional can_update on isolated current/patch observations.
  4. Commit only after all checks succeed, preserving unspecified fields.

Delete must apply full entity and transition validation with status=DELETED before committing. Repeated deletion returns INVALID. Identity uniqueness remains reserved, including after expiration and deletion.

Store { namespace, code } without delimiter collisions; namespace/code can contain NUL. Declare the serializer's supported metadata types: Core's raw cyclic-table snapshots do not imply that JSON or a database can serialize those graphs. Input and returned values must not alias storage.

An external storage adapter needs real transactions, locking, CAS or an equivalent atomic mechanism. Unprotected get/modify/set does not satisfy the contract; Interactor performs no update/delete pre-read. InMemory's guarantee is limited to non-yielding operations within one Lua VM.

docs.title: Conditional commits and caching
docs.text:
can_update rejection is INVALID; it is not automatic stale-read detection. An external adapter may support host-specific opaque ctx conditions and return CONFLICT on a CAS mismatch. Core adds no revision field or conditional-update framework. Test and document that optional capability separately.

A cache decorator implements the same Repository port. It owns invalidation, negative entries, stale refill races and post-commit invalidation failures. Caching entities lets Resolution recompute expiration from the current clock. Core provides no cache implementation or consistency guarantee; cache/real concurrency claims need adapter integration evidence.

docs.title: Register observers
docs.text:
local slds = require("slds")
local hooks = slds.Hooks.new()
hooks:on(slds.HookPoint.AFTER, function(ctx, point, value, err)
    -- Send to the host's bounded telemetry path; handle value=nil on failures.
    print(point, value ~= nil, err)
end)
hooks:on(slds.HookPoint.ON_ERROR, function(ctx, failed_point, hook_err)
    print("Hook failure", failed_point, hook_err)
end)
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(), hooks = hooks,
})

General BEFORE runs before operation-specific BEFORE; specific AFTER runs before general AFTER. Registration order applies within each point. Callbacks get the actual operation point and v0.2 arguments. All normal returns, including repository/generator errors, reach AFTER. Programming errors may propagate before AFTER.

Each observer receives an independent payload snapshot retaining domain methods and nil gaps. ctx retains its reference and should be read-only. Hooks cannot transform operations. pcall isolates exceptions, not latency; use host-managed delivery for durable or asynchronous events. ON_ERROR failure does not recurse.

docs.title: Resolve in a host
docs.text:
local function resolve_or_fallback(interactor, ctx, identity, fallback_url)
    local result, err = interactor:resolve(ctx, identity)
    if not result then return nil, err end
    if result.resolvable then return result.target end
    return fallback_url
end

The host maps result.resolvable to redirects or application behavior, maps infrastructure errors to its own failure response, and performs authorization before calling Core. Namespace is a logical identity partition, not tenant authorization. ctx propagation alone proves no access isolation.

In OpenResty, construct a worker-local Interactor in the host and acquire connections in a phase supported by the chosen client. Core has no ngx dependency. A Lua Interactor cannot be stored in ngx.shared; cross-worker persistence/uniqueness belongs to the selected adapters.

docs.title: Verify an integration
docs.text: Use a deterministic clock to test expiration just before, at and after the timestamp. Run the reusable conformance suites against fresh real adapter fixtures. Declare which evidence is sequential, deterministically interleaved or actually concurrent. Run the per-file coverage gate from fresh statistics; never substitute aggregate coverage.

docs.title: Migrating from v0.1 to v0.2
docs.text: v0.2 is a breaking public API and contract upgrade. It preserves pure Lua, zero runtime dependencies, four operations and the Identity/Lifecycle/Resolution scope. It supplies no legacy aliases or dual Hook callback formats.

docs.title: Construction and names
Resolution and time
docs.text:
Use result.resolvable to decide whether to resolve. result.found only reports existence. Expiration changes from strict < now to <= now; equality is expired. EXPIRED remains derived, never stored. Custom rules may allow DISABLED resolution, preserving DISABLED status; DELETED always remains denied.

Remove ShortLink:is_resolvable and Lifecycle.validate_transition/STATUSES usages. Use Resolution.resolve and Lifecycle's three predicates. Constructors accept partial Lifecycle overrides without modifying the supplied table; the authoritative Repository and Interactor must share effective rules.

docs.title: Writes and errors
docs.text:
Repository is the authoritative latest-state validation/commit boundary. Interactor.update/delete no longer get first. Adapters must reject stale writes to DELETED and preserve unspecified fields. Delete validates the target state as well as the transition.

Expected business errors are exactly NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID. Invalid transition, terminal update and repeat delete return nil,INVALID, rather than throwing or returning a lifecycle status. Infrastructure errors pass unchanged. Missing Repository.get returns nil,NOT_FOUND; nil,nil is now a programming error. Success plus an error is also invalid.

Unknown patch keys, including metadata, now return INVALID instead of being ignored. Namespace/code patches remain programming errors. Metadata is still captured at creation and retained through updates. Nil expires_at still means unchanged; false is INVALID. The latest architecture supplement deliberately defers expiration clearing, so issue #6's earlier clearing goal is not implemented in this release.

Create must omit status; explicit status returns INVALID. The Interactor creates ACTIVE. can_update belongs only in the authoritative Repository, runs after complete field validation, and returns a boolean. False is INVALID, not CONFLICT. External CAS can return CONFLICT, but needs its own adapter contract and evidence.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Use hooks:on(HookPoint,fn) or interactor:use({[HookPoint]=fn}). The use convenience shares the same registry and retains no old callback signatures:

interactor:use({
    [slds.HookPoint.AFTER_CREATE] = function(ctx, point, link, err)
        if link then print(point, link.code) else print(point, err) end
    end,
    [slds.HookPoint.ON_ERROR] = function(ctx, failed_point, hook_err)
        print(failed_point, hook_err)
    end,
})

Add point as the second callback argument; AFTER also receives err, and AFTER_DELETE receives ok,err. ON_ERROR receives failed_point,hook_err. BEFORE now covers generation and business validation after argument capture. Every normal success/failure reaches AFTER; handle nil values. Programming errors may still propagate without AFTER.

Ordering is general BEFORE → specific BEFORE → operation → specific AFTER → general AFTER, with registration order within each point. Per-callback payload isolation and shared read-only ctx remain. Callbacks execute synchronously; no timeout or durable-delivery guarantee is introduced.

See RFC-0002, API and validation evidence before claiming compatibility.

docs.title: Quick start tutorial · v0.2
docs.text: Build a complete short link lifecycle using the bundled reference adapters. No server or database is needed. Examples target the current v0.2 source API.

docs.title: 1. Install this checkout
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/fangfengxiang/lua-slds.git
cd lua-slds
luarocks make lua-slds-scm-1.rockspec

When reviewing an unpublished change, check out its branch before running make. Installing the package also maps bundled adapters to their documented module names.

docs.title: 2. Assemble the two ports
docs.text:
local slds = require("slds")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository")
local Composed = require("slds.adapters.composed.code_generator")
local Sequential = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator")
local Base62 = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder")

local now = 1000000
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = Repository.new(),
    code_generator = Composed.new({
        generator = Sequential.new(),
        encoders = { Base62.new() },
    }),
    clock = function() return now end,
})

Repository persists entities. CodeGenerator returns final Code; this adapter composes an instance-local counter with Base62. Core never imports either component. If all callers supply explicit codes, omit code_generator entirely.

docs.title: 3. Create
docs.text:
local ctx = {}
local generated = assert(interactor:create(ctx, { target = "https://example.com/long/path" }))
print(generated.namespace, generated.code, generated.status) -- default, 1, ACTIVE

local link = assert(interactor:create(ctx, {
    code = "welcome",
    target = "https://example.com/welcome",
    expires_at = now + 60,
    metadata = { campaign = "launch" },
}))
local identity = slds.Identity.new(link.namespace, link.code)

Namespace defaults only when omitted. Explicit Code must be a non-empty string. Omitted Code invokes the generator; invalid Code does not. New links are ACTIVE, so omit status. Target validation rejects empty values and the javascript:, data: and file: schemes; the host supplies any stricter URL policy.

docs.title: 4. Resolve and expire
docs.text:
local result = assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(result.found and result.resolvable)
assert(result.target == "https://example.com/welcome")

now = now + 60
local expired = assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(expired.found and not expired.resolvable)
assert(expired.status == slds.Resolution.EXPIRED)
assert(expired.target == nil)

Equality is already expired: expires_at <= now. The stored lifecycle remains ACTIVE. Always test result.resolvable before using target; result.found alone says only that the identity exists.

docs.title: 5. Update
docs.text:
assert(interactor:update(ctx, identity, {
    target = "https://example.com/new", expires_at = now + 3600,
}))
assert(interactor:update(ctx, identity, { status = slds.Lifecycle.DISABLED }))
assert(not assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity)).resolvable)
assert(interactor:update(ctx, identity, { status = slds.Lifecycle.ACTIVE }))

Only target/status/expires_at may be patched. Namespace/code are immutable; metadata and unknown patch fields return INVALID. Nil expiration means unchanged; there is no clearing sentinel. Repository validates and applies the sparse patch against the latest state, preserving unspecified fields.

docs.title: 6. Observe operations
docs.text:
local observed = {}
interactor:use({
    [slds.HookPoint.AFTER_RESOLVE] = function(callback_ctx, point, value, err)
        observed[#observed + 1] = { point = point, status = value and value.status, err = err }
    end,
    [slds.HookPoint.ON_ERROR] = function(callback_ctx, failed_point, hook_err)
        print("Observer failed:", failed_point, hook_err)
    end,
})
assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(observed[1].point == slds.HookPoint.AFTER_RESOLVE)

Each callback receives its own domain payload snapshot. ctx stays shared and should be treated as read-only. Observers execute synchronously; exceptions are isolated with pcall, while callback latency remains part of operation latency. AFTER also receives normal failures, so check value before accessing its fields.

docs.title: 7. Delete and handle failures
docs.text:
assert(interactor:delete(ctx, identity))
local deleted = assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(deleted.found and not deleted.resolvable)
assert(deleted.status == slds.Lifecycle.DELETED)

local again, err = interactor:delete(ctx, identity)
assert(again == nil and err == slds.Errors.INVALID)
local duplicate, conflict = interactor:create(ctx, { code = "welcome", target = "https://example.com" })
assert(duplicate == nil and conflict == slds.Errors.CONFLICT)

DELETED is terminal and reserves the identity. Expected failures use nil,err; unknown programming failures raise errors. A missing identity resolves normally to found=false/resolvable=false/status=NOT_FOUND, whereas a Repository connection failure returns nil and its original error.

Continue with the operations guide, API reference or v0.2 migration guide.

docs.title: v0.2 实现与验证记录
docs.text: 日期：2026-10-18。目标：issue #6，现行契约见 RFC-0002，兼容性变化见迁移说明。以下本地结果由本轮实际运行获得，远端结果须按具体提交单独确认。

docs.title: 实现范围
docs.text:
• 单一 Interactor 编排 create/resolve/update/delete；Core 只依赖 Repository 与可选 CodeGenerator，零新增运行时依赖。
  • Generator/Encoder 从 Core 端口移入 Adapter 组合；Composed 支持有序编码器、空数组、错误短路和最终 Code 校验。现有 Sequential/Base62 数值范围不变。
  • Lifecycle 支持构造期部分覆盖，硬身份、三状态和 DELETED 终态约束保留。Resolution 明确 found/resolvable，并在 expires_at <= now 派生 EXPIRED。
  • Repository 在最新记录上完成完整实体校验、可选 can_update 和原子提交；Interactor 更新/删除没有预读；删除也检查目标状态有效性。
  • Errors 收敛为 NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID。未知补丁和 metadata 更新返回 INVALID；不增加过期时间清除哨兵。依赖 nil,nil 或同时返回结果/错误视为编程错误。
  • Hooks 使用 HookPoint 有序函数数组、统一 v0.2 签名与独立快照；所有正常返回都触发 AFTER。use(hook) 复用同一注册表。

docs.title: 证据边界
docs.text:
• InMemory 原子性限定为单 Lua VM 内不 yield 的操作。顺序测试与可控交错不能证明真实数据库并发或跨进程唯一性。
  • ctx 原样传递不代表租户隔离或鉴权。没有缓存实现，所以没有缓存失效证据。外部 CAS、缓存和宿主权限需要自己的集成测试。
  • Hook 是同步观察者；pcall 不保证超时、非阻塞、沙箱或持久事件。ctx 和非 table 资源内部状态仍由宿主管理。
  • metadata 原始图快照支持环/共享子表，但不承诺外部 JSON/数据库可以序列化相同内容。未知补丁现在返回 INVALID。
  • 最新补充明确暂不引入清除哨兵，因此 issue #6 的早期 expires_at 清除目标延期，不能声称已经完成。

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text: This document indexes architectural decisions. ADR-012 defines the current v0.2 changes; historical portions of ADR-008/011 are explicitly superseded. See RFC-0002.

docs.title: Decision Index
docs.text: # Title Status Date ADR-001 Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-002 EXPIRED as Derived State (Not Persisted) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-003 ResolutionResult Instead of ShortLink Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-004 Code Immutability After Creation Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-005 Logical Delete (No Physical Removal) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-006 Hooks Isolation via pcall Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-007 Zero Core Dependencies (Pure Lua) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-008 Generator/Encoder Separation Superseded at Core boundary by ADR-012 2026-10-08 ADR-009 Error Handling Three-Class System Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-010 Conformance Test Suite as Specification Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-011 Contract hardening and evidence boundaries Partly superseded by ADR-012 2026-10-18 ADR-012 v0.2 minimal API and authoritative writes Accepted 2026-10-18

docs.title: ADR-001: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS needs to support multiple storage backends (Redis, MySQL, in-memory) and runtime environments (plain Lua, OpenResty). The domain logic must remain stable regardless of infrastructure choices.

Decision: Use hexagonal architecture. The domain core depends on port interfaces (Repository and optional CodeGenerator in v0.2). Adapters implement these ports. The domain never imports an adapter directly.

Consequences: - (+) Domain logic is infrastructure-agnostic - (+) Adapters can be swapped without domain changes - (+) Domain is fully testable with mock/in-memory adapters - (-) Slightly more boilerplate (port definitions + adapter implementations)

docs.title: ADR-002: EXPIRED as Derived State (Not Persisted)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Short links can have an optional expires_at timestamp. When expired, resolution should return "not resolvable". Should EXPIRED be a persistent status stored in the repository, or a derived state computed at resolution time?

Decision: EXPIRED is derived at resolution time, not stored as a persistent status. Only three statuses are persisted: ACTIVE, DISABLED, DELETED.

Rationale: Storing EXPIRED as a persistent status would require: - A background scanner to periodically check and update expired records - A scheduler dependency in the domain (violates RULE-001/RULE-002) - Race conditions between the scanner and concurrent resolution

Deriving EXPIRED at resolution time (expires_at <= now in v0.2) is O(1), requires no background process, and is always accurate.

Consequences: - (+) No background process needed - (+) Always accurate (checked at query time) - (+) No scheduler dependency in Core - (-) expires_at must be stored and indexed if query-by-status is needed

docs.title: ADR-003: ResolutionResult Instead of ShortLink
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: The resolve operation returns link information to the caller. Should it return the internal ShortLink entity or a separate ResolutionResult?

Decision: Return ResolutionResult, a stable contract that does not expose the internal ShortLink entity.

Rationale: Returning the raw entity would leak persistence details. If ShortLink's schema changes, all consumers would break. ResolutionResult is a stable contract with a defined field set.

Consequences: - (+) Internal entity schema can evolve without breaking consumers - (+) Clear distinction between "raw data" (ShortLink) and "resolution outcome" (ResolutionResult) - (-) Extra mapping layer in Resolution.resolve()

docs.title: ADR-004: Code Immutability After Creation
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Can the code field of a ShortLink be changed after creation?

Decision: Code is immutable after creation. The update operation rejects patches that include namespace or code.

Rationale: Changing the code would invalidate all existing short URLs pointing to the old code. It would also violate the uniqueness contract (the old code is now free, the new code might conflict). Immutability simplifies caching, indexing, and auditing.

Consequences: - (+) Short URLs are permanent once created - (+) Cache invalidation is simpler (code never changes) - (+) Audit trail is clean - (-) Cannot "rename" a short link (must delete + create new)

docs.title: ADR-005: Logical Delete (No Physical Removal)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: When a short link is deleted, should the record be physically removed from the repository?

Decision: Delete is logical — sets status to DELETED (terminal). The record remains in the repository. Deleted codes MUST NOT be reused (RULE-006).

Rationale: - Audit trail: deleted links may need to be tracked for compliance - Collision prevention: reusing a deleted code would redirect old references to a new target - Terminal state: DELETED has no outgoing transitions in the state machine

Consequences: - (+) Retained identity/tombstone; full audit history remains a host concern - (+) No accidental code reuse - (-) Reserved identities consume storage; archival must retain uniqueness reservations

docs.title: ADR-006: Hooks Isolation via pcall
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Hooks (Logger, Metrics, Tracer) are user-provided extensions. If a hook fails, should the operation fail?

Decision: Hooks are isolated via pcall. A failing hook triggers on_error callbacks without failing the operation. Callbacks remain synchronous and add latency; see ADR-011 for observer snapshots and guarantee boundaries.

Rationale: Hooks are observability extensions, not domain logic (RULE-007, RULE-008). A broken logger should not prevent a successful resolution. The pcall isolation is applied to each hook callback independently, and on_error itself is also isolated (double isolation).

Consequences: - (+) Hook exceptions do not abort operations; callback latency remains a host concern - (+) Hook exceptions are isolated; host code remains responsible for callback latency and side effects - (-) Silent failures (mitigated by on_error callback)

docs.title: ADR-007: Zero Core Dependencies (Pure Lua)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS Core needs to run in multiple environments (plain Lua 5.1/5.3, LuaJIT, OpenResty). Should it depend on any external libraries?

Decision: Core layer has zero external dependencies. Only pure Lua stdlib is used. No ngx, redis, mysql, cjson, or any third-party Lua rock.

Rationale: A domain specification library should be as portable as possible. Depending on cjson or ngx would limit the environments where Core can run. The protocol/codec libraries that SLDS is modeled after (dkjson, lua-MessagePack) are also pure Lua.

Consequences: - (+) Maximum portability - (+) Easy to test (no mocking of external deps) - (+) Clear boundary between Core and Infrastructure - (-) Some convenience features (e.g., JSON encoding of metadata) must be done by the host

docs.title: ADR-008: Generator/Encoder Separation
docs.text:
Status: Historical Core-port decision, superseded by ADR-012. Components remain separate inside adapters.

Context: Short code generation involves two concerns: uniqueness (ensuring no two links share a code) and encoding (producing a URL-safe string). Should these be combined into one port or separated?

Decision: Separate into two ports: Generator (produces internal unique ID) and Encoder (transforms ID to short code string).

Rationale: - Uniqueness is an infrastructure concern (needs atomicity, possibly distributed coordination) - Encoding is a pure transformation (no I/O, deterministic, mathematical) - Separation allows swapping either independently (e.g., sequential → snowflake generator, Base62 → hash encoder)

Consequences: - (+) Independent evolution of uniqueness strategy and encoding format - (+) Encoder is trivially testable (pure function) - (-) Two ports instead of one (minor complexity)

docs.title: ADR-009: Error Handling Three-Class System
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS needs a consistent error handling strategy. When should it use error() vs return nil, err vs pcall?

Decision: Three-class error handling:

  1. Runtime errors → return nil, err (repository failures, not found, conflicts)
  2. Programming errors → error(msg, 2) (invalid arguments, immutable field violation)
  3. Hook exception isolation → pcall (user hook callbacks); expected port failures return nil,err and unexpected port programming errors propagate.

Rationale: This follows the Lua ecosystem convention (lua-resty-redis, lua-resty-http, dkjson). Runtime errors are expected conditions the caller should handle. Programming errors are bugs that should fail fast. Third-party code is isolated to prevent crashes.

Consequences: - (+) Callers can distinguish "expected failures" from "bugs" - (+) Fail-fast for programming errors prevents silent corruption - (+) Hook exceptions do not fail operations; port programming errors remain visible - (-) Slightly more cognitive load (three patterns instead of one)

docs.title: ADR-010: Conformance Test Suite as Specification
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS is a specification, not just a library. Multiple implementations may exist (reference implementation, Redis-backed, MySQL-backed). How do we ensure they all comply?

Decision: The Conformance Test Suite (L0-L3) is the specification enforcement mechanism. Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass the applicable test suite (RULE-010).

Test levels:

Level Scope L0 Core: create/resolve/update/delete L1 Lifecycle: expiration, disabled, terminal delete, code reuse L2 Duplicate rejection, commit order, deterministic interleavings and atomicity; external concurrency requires adapter evidence L3 Metadata, hooks, context propagation and visibility; cache/tenant extensions require host integration evidence

Consequences: - (+) Objective compatibility verification - (+) Tests serve as executable specification - (+) New implementations can self-verify applicable scenarios and identify outstanding evidence - (-) Test suite must be maintained alongside the spec

docs.title: ADR-011: Contract hardening and evidence boundaries
docs.text:
Status: Historical v0.1 hardening (2026-10-18). ADR-012 supersedes terminal error codes and the public API; snapshot and evidence principles remain accepted.

  • Preserve ordinary Lua tables and logical identity immutability; update APIs and stored snapshots protect persistent identity, not arbitrary direct assignments.
  • Apply sparse patches atomically against the latest record using domain rules. Reject updates to DELETED at commit with nil,DELETED; different fields survive, the same field follows commit order. This does not provide application read-modify-write conflict detection.
  • Copy raw metadata table graphs on domain/storage boundaries, omit metadata metatables, and retain non-table leaves. Metadata updates and deep merge remain unsupported.
  • Hooks are synchronous observers with per-callback domain snapshots. Exception isolation is not latency isolation, sandboxing or durable delivery; ctx stays host-owned.
  • Sequential/Base62 numeric limits belong only to the bundled adapters. Generic ports remain representation-agnostic; the host selects compatible pairs.
  • Factory-driven conformance runs real reference adapters and labels sequential/interleaving evidence honestly. No real database concurrency, cache invalidation or tenant isolation claim follows from this run.
  • Every production Lua file must reach 95% line coverage independently in each supported CI interpreter. No file exclusions or stale statistics may hide a gap.

docs.title: ADR-012: v0.2 minimal API and authoritative writes
docs.text:
Status: Accepted (2026-10-18).

Context: Issue #6 and its later architecture supplement seek a coherent public API without expanding SLDS beyond Identity/Lifecycle/Resolution. Core only needs final Code, and a Core pre-read cannot validate the state present at atomic commit time.

Decision:

  • Rename the sole four-operation orchestrator to Interactor. Export named modules rather than flat aliases. Do not add operation containers or managers.
  • Expose Repository and optional CodeGenerator as the only Core ports. Keep Generator/Encoder as adapter components, with a small Composed reference adapter; retain their existing numeric limits only in those components.
  • Let authoritative Repository validate/commit latest-state sparse writes, with no Interactor update/delete pre-read. Full candidate validation precedes optional can_update. Delete checks target validity and transition. Rule/terminal rejection returns INVALID; genuine conditional-commit conflicts remain CONFLICT.
  • Normalize partial Lifecycle functions at construction through one small internal helper. Hard identity, known-status and terminal constraints remain protected.
  • Add ResolutionResult.resolvable and expire at expires_at <= now. Keep EXPIRED derived and outside Errors. Errors is exactly NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID.
  • Reject unknown Patch fields, including metadata. Keep nil expiration unchanged; defer clearing instead of inventing a sentinel contrary to the latest supplement.
  • Use point-indexed ordered Hook callbacks with v0.2 signatures. Keep Interactor:use(hook) as a convenience into the same registry. BEFORE covers complete valid use cases and AFTER observes every normal outcome.

Consequences: The upgrade is intentionally breaking and has explicit migration notes. No compatibility dispatcher, new runtime dependency, cache/CAS implementation or generic policy/pipeline framework is introduced. Existing table snapshots, pure Lua conventions and per-file coverage/evidence gates remain. Validation reports actual checks independently of this decision.

docs.title: Design rationale · v0.2
docs.text: SLDS answers three questions: which short link is this, which lifecycle changes are valid, and may this link resolve now? A capability belongs in Core only when it is necessary to answer those questions or provide the smallest explicit integration boundary.

docs.title: Ask for the final value
docs.text:
Create needs Code, not an internal counter/UUID and an encoder. Repository and optional CodeGenerator are therefore the only Core ports. Adapter authors can compose generator/encoder components without making every caller configure them. Explicit-code creation works with Repository alone. No new algorithm, registry or generic pipeline framework is needed.

Sequential/Base62 remain useful reference components. Their numeric limits are documented at the adapter level, leaving Core free to accept a non-empty string of any representation or length supported by the host.

docs.title: Validate where the latest state exists
docs.text:
A Core pre-read cannot establish the state present when a database write commits. Interactor.update/delete therefore call the write port directly. Repository applies the same domain value/transition rules to its latest record under an atomic commit mechanism. Sparse patches preserve unrelated concurrent changes; failed validation cannot partially write or revive DELETED.

can_update is a small repository-local business predicate, not a policy engine or automatic stale-read detector. Complete field validation runs first, so invalid expiration values cannot turn an ordinary comparison into an accidental programming exception. Optional CAS remains an adapter/host contract with separate concurrency evidence.

docs.title: Keep time derived
docs.text:
Only ACTIVE, DISABLED and DELETED are stored. Expiration is computed at resolution time using expires_at <= now. Persisting EXPIRED would require scheduled state transitions and complicate extending expiration. Resolution remains pure and storage-free; Repository.get alone cannot tell a host whether it may redirect now.

found and resolvable answer different questions. A disabled/deleted/expired identity can exist while being unresolvable. Custom rules may permit DISABLED, so comparing status to ACTIVE is less reliable than checking resolvable.

docs.title: Extend without weakening invariants
docs.text:
Lifecycle overrides supply three functions, with partial defaults resolved at construction. Hard identity, known-status and terminal guards remain independent of those functions. This allows host-specific restrictions without introducing new status types or a general rule system.

Metadata stays opaque. Raw-table snapshots preserve table ownership without adding serialization, deep merge or freezing. Unknown patches return INVALID rather than silently accepting an operation that had no effect. Expiration clearing is deferred because the latest design requires no sentinel in this version.

docs.title: Observe without controlling the operation
docs.text:
Hooks registers ordered functions by explicit point. General/specific phases make ordering deterministic. BEFORE covers valid calls before generation and business validation; AFTER sees every normal outcome, including failures.

Each observer gets independent domain payloads; ctx remains shared and should be read-only. pcall prevents one observer exception from breaking an operation. It cannot bound callback latency, make delivery durable or protect shared host resources. The host must provide those capabilities if needed.

docs.title: Use Lua conventions and measure claims
docs.text:
Shared class metatables, dot factories, colon methods and explicit construction keep the implementation familiar on Lua 5.1/5.3/LuaJIT. Normalized rules and point-indexed Hook arrays avoid unnecessary work; no I/O pre-read is needed for update/delete. Performance multipliers are not claimed without benchmarks.

Each production file needs fresh independent coverage >=95%; aggregate coverage is insufficient. Real reference adapters power conformance. Sequential tests and controlled interleavings demonstrate defined scenarios, not external database concurrency, cache invalidation or tenant authorization. See validation records and architecture decisions.

docs.title: Domain layer architecture · v0.2
docs.text: The domain layer defines identity, lifecycle and resolution behavior with no infrastructure I/O. Interactor coordinates four operations; Repository owns the atomic validation/commit boundary for writes.

docs.title: Objects and responsibilities
docs.text:
Module Responsibility Identity Non-empty namespace/code tuple, logical immutability and value equality ShortLink Validated entity, sparse patches and independent metadata snapshots Lifecycle Three persistent statuses and three default predicates Resolution Pure existence/resolvability/expiration decision and result Errors NOT_FOUND / CONFLICT / INVALID

Identity uses ordinary Lua tables with a shared class metatable. Callers must not assign identity fields. No proxy/freeze framework is introduced. The tuple is distinct from host, URL, tenant or storage key.

ShortLink contains target/status/expires_at/metadata in addition to identity. Only target/status/expires_at can be patched. Unknown fields including metadata return INVALID; immutable identity patches raise an error. Metadata is opaque raw-table data, captured independently across entity/export/storage boundaries. Cycles and alias relationships inside a snapshot survive; metatables do not. Persistence adapters may support a narrower serializable subset.

docs.title: Lifecycle and rules
docs.text:
Persistent statuses are ACTIVE, DISABLED and DELETED. Defaults allow ACTIVE↔DISABLED and ACTIVE/DISABLED→DELETED. DELETED has no outgoing transitions and remains reserved. Same-status patches do not invoke the transition predicate.

Constructors normalize a partial rule table into is_valid/can_transition/is_resolvable defaults without modifying it. A small internal function shares this normalization; it is not a policy manager or new public API. Direct domain calls may use partial rules. Hosts must configure consistent rules in Interactor and Repository.

Custom rules cannot authorize unknown persistent statuses, revival or DELETED resolution. is_valid may restrict states, and can_transition may restrict changes. Custom is_resolvable can permit DISABLED, but expiration and terminal safeguards remain.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution reads no storage and writes nothing. Repository.get supplies an independent ShortLink; Resolution applies absence, DELETED, custom denial, expiration and success in that order.

ResolutionResult = {
    found, resolvable, namespace, code,
    target?, status, expires_at?
}

Target appears only when resolvable. The actual persistent status survives successful custom resolution. expires_at <= now derives Resolution.EXPIRED without changing the stored entity; no timer or scheduler is needed. NOT_FOUND is a normal absence result, while infrastructure failure remains nil,err.

docs.title: Write authority
docs.text:
The entity defines valid values and transitions. The authoritative Repository must apply those same domain rules to its latest state inside the atomic write boundary. It is responsible for uniqueness, terminal guards, optional can_update and rollback, while Resolution remains responsible for time-dependent read semantics.

Interactor.update/delete do not get first. The repository validates complete candidate fields before can_update; policy observation must not change committed data. Delete also uses full entity/transition validation, including custom validity of DELETED.

docs.title: Lua implementation
docs.text:
Factories use dot notation; instance methods use colon notation; instances share their class metatable. Expected business failures return nil,err, programming errors throw, and only Hook callbacks are exception-isolated. Domain modules depend only on other pure Lua domain/internal helpers. No adapter, ngx, database, JSON or HTTP module is imported.

See RFC-0002, API and ports/adapters.

docs.title: Ports and adapters · v0.2
docs.text:
Core requests behavior through two duck-typed contracts. It never imports a concrete adapter. The host explicitly constructs Repository, optional CodeGenerator and Interactor; ctx carries opaque per-call host data, not dependency discovery.

flowchart TD Host --> Interactor Interactor --> Domain[Identity / ShortLink / Lifecycle / Resolution] Interactor --> Hooks[Hooks + HookPoint] Interactor --> Repository Interactor --> CodeGenerator[CodeGenerator optional] InMemory -. implements .-> Repository External[External storage adapter] -. implements .-> Repository Composed -. implements .-> CodeGenerator Composed --> Generator Generator --> Encoders[Ordered Encoder array]

docs.title: Repository
docs.text:
Repository provides create/get/update/delete. Get retrieves an independent entity, leaving read-time resolvability to Resolution. Writes enforce identity uniqueness, latest-state validation, sparse fields and terminal deletion atomically. Failure cannot partially commit. Deleted/expired identities do not become reusable.

Interactor performs no update/delete pre-read. The repository validates a complete candidate, then optional can_update, then commits under the storage's atomic mechanism. can_update=false is INVALID. Delete validates both target-state validity and transition. External storage needs its own transaction/lock/CAS implementation; Core cannot make an unprotected get/modify/set atomic.

The bundled InMemory adapter uses a nested namespace/code map, independent metadata snapshots and non-yielding writes within one Lua VM. It proves neither cross-process uniqueness nor concurrent database behavior. External cache decorators implement the same port and own their consistency model.

docs.title: CodeGenerator
docs.text:
CodeGenerator.generate(ctx,input) returns final Code. Code is the only representation Core needs; it does not need an internal ID, encoder alphabet or numeric domain. Callers supplying explicit valid Code need no generator. Missing Code invokes the optional port; invalid explicit Code is rejected directly.

Composed is a reference adapter, not a new Core framework. It calls generator.generate(ctx), followed by an ordered dense array of encoder.encode(value). Intermediate values remain opaque. Empty encoder arrays work when the generator already returns Code. Failure stops immediately; final output must be a non-empty string.

Sequential and Base62 remain replaceable components inside that adapter. Their exact integer domain [0,2^53-1] and Sequential's instance-local uniqueness/exhaustion do not constrain generic CodeGenerator. Full uint64 or string identifiers need compatible external components without lossy tonumber coercion.

docs.title: Keep integrations outside Core
docs.text:
Host or adapter concern Why it stays outside Core HTTP/OpenResty Transport does not define identity or resolution Redis/Postgres connections Storage-specific resource and atomicity mechanisms Cache invalidation Adapter-specific consistency and failure model Authorization/tenant policy Namespace and ctx are not access control Telemetry delivery Hook observation does not supply queues or durability CAS/version fields Optional adapter/host condition, not a universal domain value

The API specifies method responses; the operations guide explains integration; conformance defines the evidence an adapter must supply.

docs.title: v0.2 implementation plan
docs.text: Spec: v0.2-proposal.md, issue #6 and the user's two API/architecture attachments. The user has resumed the original implementation/test/GitHub CI objective. Branch: codex/v02-api-contracts. Baseline: 4465fa7.

docs.title: Resolved contract choices
docs.text:
• Follow the later attachment: no expiration-clearing sentinel; rule/terminal rejection returns INVALID; unknown Patch keys are rejected; BEFORE covers the complete valid use case.
  • Keep issue #6's interactor:use(hook) convenience registration, accepting a table keyed by HookPoint values. It registers the same v0.2 callbacks as Hooks:on(point,fn); it does not preserve v0.1 callback argument positions or add a second dispatcher.
  • Use a small internal/lifecycle.lua resolver so partial rules are normalized once per constructor without exposing a new stable Lifecycle API or mutating host tables. Direct pure domain calls can use defaults or partial functions without allocating a new rules table on each call.
  • Preserve only Interactor as the orchestration module. Root exports use Lifecycle/Errors namespaces; no old Service or flat aliases.
  • CAS/cache remain optional external Adapter capabilities. Document the issue's expiration-clearing difference explicitly; do not claim external concurrency or clear-time support.

docs.title: Global constraints
docs.text: Pure Lua 5.1/5.3/LuaJIT, zero runtime dependencies, four use cases, two Core ports, shared class metatables, explicit construction, atomic authority writes, independent metadata/hook snapshots, every production file >=95% from fresh LuaCov data. Preserve docs/report.md. OpenSpec remains ignored locally. Draft PR only; do not merge main.

First write failing tests for partial overrides, closed errors, <= expiry, terminal guards, unknown patches, policy/transition rejection and rollback; then implement and run the focused tests.

docs.title: Interface dependencies
docs.text:
Domain produces ShortLink.new(data,rules), link:with_patch(patch,rules), Resolution.resolve(link,id,now,rules), and internal rule normalization. Repository consumes Domain. Interactor consumes Repository, CodeGenerator:generate(ctx,input), Hooks:before/after and HookPoint; it never imports adapters. Fixture uses real InMemory plus composed Sequential/Base62. Hooks preserve domain root metatables while cloning payload contents.

Tasks share interfaces, not file ownership. Agents do not commit independently or edit another task's files. Focused red/green logs and final review findings are recorded in the validation report; controller integrates and owns the single final Git delivery.

docs.title: lua-slds v0.2 架构与公共 API 提案
docs.text:
状态：已收敛并实施，交付验证中。日期：2026-10-18。基准提交：4465fa7。

依据：issue #6、用户提供的《公共 API 与模块架构整理》及后续《架构重构方案》。后续补充优先；用户恢复最初的实施、测试和 GitHub CI 要求后，按第 12 节收敛差异。

本设计记录 v0.2 的定位、取舍与实现契约。实现和测试位于 codex/v02-api-contracts 独立分支，以 Draft PR 供整体评审，不合并 main。验证结果见 验证记录。

docs.title: 1. 从项目定位判断改动价值
docs.text:
SLDS 的核心仍是 Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics。建议继续称为纯 Lua 短链领域规范及参考类库；Interactor 是四个用例的编排对象，不把项目定位扩大为通用“用例执行框架”。

本轮最有价值的改变有三项：Core 只索取最终 Code；写入规则收敛到权威 Repository 的原子提交边界；Resolution 明确给出 resolvable。它们分别减少算法绑定、陈旧预读和调用方重复判断。

Service 改名 Interactor、HookPoint 和根导出整理属于接口一致性改进，不应独立成为继续拆模块的理由。保留现有实体快照、身份元组、纯 Lua 实现和测试设施。

遵守 RFC-0001 的十条铁律，尤其是 RULE-001/002/003 的基础设施隔离、RULE-004/005/006 的身份与持久化约束、RULE-007/008 的观察者边界、RULE-009 的宿主鉴权及 RULE-010 的符合性证据。

docs.title: 2. 推荐范围与明确排除
docs.text:
推荐一次有版本边界的 v0.2 契约升级：Interactor、两个 Core Port、可注入 Lifecycle、CodeGenerator 组合适配器、明确的解析结果、按运行点分组的同步 Hooks。

本轮不实现 Redis/Postgres/CachedRepository、Snowflake/UUID/64 位编码器、缓存一致性协议、Outbox、消息队列、DI Container、全局 Registry、规则引擎或通用 Pipeline 框架。不增加批量 API、get 用例、quickGet、版本字段或 metadata 深合并。

三个方案的取舍：

方案 收益 代价 建议 仅修 v0.1，不改入口与 Port 迁移小 无法支持无需双生成器的创建方式，接口歧义保留 不满足此次目标 收敛 v0.2 契约，复用现有模块和工具 解除绑定，写入与解析职责清楚 有明确破坏性变更 推荐 同时建设缓存、策略与通用执行框架 更多基础设施能力 偏离领域定位，测试与依赖面显著扩大 不纳入

docs.title: 3. v0.1 基线逐文件盘点
docs.text:
改造前 15 个生产 Lua 文件均有 LuaCov 100% 行覆盖率；此结果是 v0.1 基线，不是 v0.2 已实现的证据。下表的测试文件省略 spec/ 前缀。

当前文件 实际职责与依赖 现有测试 v0.2 建议 src/slds/init.lua 导出 Domain/Hooks、new 和扁平常量；加载 Service public_api_spec、service_spec new 转向 Interactor；新增 Interactor/HookPoint；收敛常量出口 src/slds/service.lua 编排四操作；依赖 Domain/Hooks；强制 generator+encoder；更新删除有预读 service_spec、service_boundaries_spec、L0–L3 迁为 interactor.lua；更新删除只调用一次 Repository 写方法 src/slds/hooks.lua 插件对象列表、运行点字符串拼接、pcall、独立领域快照 hooks_spec、hook_observation_spec、L3 改为按 HookPoint 索引的有序函数数组，保留隔离保障 src/slds/internal/snapshot.lua 复制原始 table 图，保留环与共享子表，去掉元表 value_boundaries_spec、Hook/metadata 测试 保留；不变成通用冻结工具 src/slds/domain/identity.lua 元组构造、默认 namespace、值相等、字符串表示；不依赖 Port identity_spec、入口与 Hook 测试 保留普通 table 的逻辑不可变约定 src/slds/domain/lifecycle.lua 固定三状态和转换矩阵；validate_transition 抛异常 lifecycle_spec、L1 增加 is_valid，接受覆盖规则，移除 validate_transition src/slds/domain/short_link.lua 字段校验、稀疏补丁、metadata 快照；当前还判断可解析性 short_link_spec、value_boundaries_spec 接收 Lifecycle；移除 is_resolvable；未知补丁拒绝 src/slds/domain/resolution.lua 纯解析结果与决策，依赖 Lifecycle/Errors；当前无 resolvable resolution_spec、L0/L1 增加 resolvable；等值过期；使用注入规则 src/slds/domain/errors.lua 当前混合操作错误与解析状态 public_api_spec、领域/合规测试 仅保留 NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID src/slds/ports/repository.lua 四方法契约桩；不提供具体实现 public_api_spec、L0–L3 保留方法；明确最新状态校验与失败契约 src/slds/ports/generator.lua 内部 ID 生成端口桩 public_api_spec 从 Core 移除；算法组件约定移至适配器文档 src/slds/ports/encoder.lua ID 到 Code 的端口桩 public_api_spec 从 Core 移除；保留适配器内部编码组件 adapters/inmemory/repository.lua 二层元组映射、独立快照、无 yield 原子操作；删除直接改状态 reference_adapters_spec、真实 fixture 合规测试 注入规则与 can_update；删除也校验转换 adapters/sequential/generator.lua 实例内递增整数、范围与耗尽行为 reference_adapters_spec、fixture_spec 保留，作为组合生成器的内部组件 adapters/base62/encoder.lua 安全整数范围的确定性 Base62 encoder_spec、reference_adapters_spec 保留，不隐式支持完整 uint64

基线实际 require 关系是 Service 依赖 Domain、Hooks、snapshot；Hooks 也依赖 Identity/ShortLink/Resolution 和 snapshot；具体 Adapter 可依赖 Domain。基线尚无 Interactor。Port 是鸭子类型契约，不必让 Domain require Port 桩。第 4 节是目标逻辑契约图，不能将其误写成当前源码已有的 require 链。

改造前测试入口共 17 个：13 个顶层 *_spec.lua、4 个合规入口；另有 helpers.lua 与 4 个可复用合规模块。总计 209 项测试。迁移时保留边界测试含义，不为重排目录机械搬迁所有测试。

新增生产模块为 interactor.lua、hook_point.lua、ports/code_generator.lua、adapters/composed/code_generator.lua；同时移除旧 Service 和两个旧 Core Port，共享归一化采用内部函数模块后，实际从 15 个变为 17 个生产模块，没有引入管理器。

docs.title: 4. 目标架构与公共入口
docs.text:
flowchart TD Host[宿主显式组装] --> I[Interactor：四个领域操作] I --> D[Domain：Identity / ShortLink / Lifecycle / Resolution / Errors] I --> H[Hooks + HookPoint] I --> R[Repository 契约] I --> G[可选 CodeGenerator 契约] RA[Repository Adapter] -.实现.-> R GA[组合 CodeGenerator Adapter] -.实现.-> G RA --> D GA --> C[内部 Generator → Encoder 数组]

根模块建议公开 VERSION、new、Interactor、Identity、ShortLink、Lifecycle、Resolution、Errors、Hooks、HookPoint。不导出 Port 桩或参考 Adapter；移除现有扁平状态/错误别名。不增加 Operations/Statuses 重复命名空间，见评审项 R2。

local slds = require('slds')
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = repository,          -- 必需；由宿主构造
    code_generator = code_generator,  -- 可选；Core 不自动装配
    lifecycle = lifecycle,            -- 可选；允许局部覆盖
    clock = clock,                    -- 默认 os.time
    hooks = hooks,                    -- 默认空注册表
})

local link, err = interactor:create(ctx, input)
local result, err = interactor:resolve(ctx, identity)
local updated, err = interactor:update(ctx, identity, patch)
local ok, err = interactor:delete(ctx, identity)

不从 ctx 定位依赖；ctx 原样传递，Core 不解释宿主资源或业务键。new 与 Interactor.new 使用同一个构造实现。

docs.title: 5. 领域规则与实体
docs.text:
Lifecycle 只保留 ACTIVE/DISABLED/DELETED 三种持久状态，以及 is_valid(status)、can_transition(from,to)、is_resolvable(status) 三个纯谓词。默认转换矩阵延续 v0.1；同状态补丁不调用转换谓词。业务非法转换返回 nil,Errors.INVALID。

允许部分覆盖，缺项采用默认函数；不能修改用户传入的表。Interactor 与权威 Repository 必须使用同一套有效函数，运行期不重新合并或修改配置。归一化只发生在组装期，不能在解析热路径持续分配规则表。

共享归一化采用 internal/lifecycle.lua 小型函数模块，供 Interactor 与 Repository 构造时复用。公共 Lifecycle 仍只提供三个谓词，不暴露内部归一化函数。直接领域调用按需读取覆盖函数，不在热路径合并规则表。

硬不变量不能被自定义函数放宽：身份不可改名、未知持久状态不合法、DELETED 不可恢复/解析、删除身份不可复用。is_valid 只能进一步限制三个合法状态；can_transition/is_resolvable 即使错误地返回 true，也不能绕过终态。

ShortLink.new(data,lifecycle)、link:with_patch(patch,lifecycle)、is_expired(now)、to_table() 保留。移除 link:is_resolvable(now)，解析只走 Resolution。新建记录的状态由 Interactor 固定为 ACTIVE；建议拒绝 create 输入中的显式 status，避免看似生效但被忽略。

补丁建议只允许 target/status/expires_at。namespace/code 属于编程错误；metadata 和其他未知字段返回 INVALID，不静默忽略。metadata 仍创建时持久化、后续保留，不增加更新或合并语义。

根据最新补充，nil expires_at 表示未提供，false 也不是清除哨兵；暂不提供清除功能。这与 issue 的清除语义目标尚未一致，见 R1，不能声称已完成该项。

metadata 继续复制原始 table 图；不执行/运输元表，非 table 叶子按原值保留。真实持久化格式可支持更窄的数据集，Adapter 必须验证并说明；Core 支持循环 table 快照，不代表 JSON/数据库支持相同数据。

docs.title: 6. Resolution 与错误
docs.text:
Resolution.resolve(link,identity,now,lifecycle) 只做纯领域判断，返回独立结果：found、resolvable、namespace、code、target、status、expires_at。

判定顺序 found resolvable status target 无记录 false false NOT_FOUND nil DELETED true false DELETED nil 注入规则不允许解析 true false 实际持久状态 nil expires_at <= now true false EXPIRED nil 可以解析 true true 实际持久状态 原目标

只有 resolvable 是宿主判断能否跳转的标准字段。若自定义规则允许 DISABLED 解析，结果须保留 DISABLED，不能改写成 ACTIVE；DELETED 和过期仍有硬保护。过期不写回 Repository。now 与 expires_at 仍要求有限数值。

Errors 仅包含 NOT_FOUND、CONFLICT、INVALID。EXPIRED 归于 Resolution.EXPIRED；DISABLED/DELETED 使用 Lifecycle 常量。

情形 返回 业务成功 result,nil 创建身份重复、Adapter 条件提交冲突 nil,Errors.CONFLICT 非法字段/转换、can_update 拒绝、终态更新或重复删除 nil,Errors.INVALID update/delete 不存在 nil,Errors.NOT_FOUND resolve 不存在 正常 NOT_FOUND ResolutionResult，err=nil 基础设施故障 nil,原始 err 编程错误或依赖违约 error(msg,2)，不伪装成业务失败

Repository/CodeGenerator 返回 nil,nil 属于依赖违约；不再当作不存在。稳定错误码不拼接前缀。建议同样识别 result 与 err 同时非 nil 的违约。Core 不用 xpcall 包住整个用例，编程异常不保证 AFTER。

docs.title: 7. Repository 与条件提交
docs.text:
只保留 create/get/update/delete。Interactor 的 update/delete 捕获参数后直接调用一次写方法，不先 get，也不先执行 with_patch。权威 Adapter 在自己的原子提交范围内完成最新读取、规则检查、提交和结果快照。

更新流程：定位最新记录 → 不存在 NOT_FOUND → DELETED INVALID → with_patch 完整校验字段/键/转换并生成候选实体 → can_update → 提交。策略只接收字段值已经验证的原始稀疏补丁，不能把候选实体的全量字段当作补丁。这样普通数值比较策略不会因为收到字符串 expires_at 而把 INVALID 变成异常；非法补丁不调用 can_update。

can_update(current,patch) 只注入权威 Repository，不注入 Interactor 或实体。它是纯、同步、不 yield 的布尔谓词：false 返回 INVALID，非布尔返回或异常是编程错误，事务必须回滚。传给谓词的观察值不得被其修改后带入实际提交。

删除也必须在最新状态上复用实体变换，例如 with_patch({status=DELETED},rules)，同时校验目标状态有效性及 can_transition(current,DELETED)。任何拒绝返回 INVALID；重复删除返回 INVALID。不能只检查转换而绕过自定义 is_valid，写出随后无法重建的记录。成功后保留身份占用。can_update 不负责删除，避免产生第二套删除策略入口。

不同字段的稀疏更新保留彼此结果；同字段按提交顺序生效。这不等于自动识别应用层陈旧读改写。v0.2 不增加通用 revision/if_match 字段；外部 Adapter 可使用宿主约定的 opaque ctx 条件执行 CAS，失败返回 CONFLICT。该能力必须单独给出并发证据，不能用 can_update 的一般业务拒绝冒充 CAS。

缓存装饰器保持同一 Port，Core 不认识 L1/L2 或失效方法。推荐缓存实体快照，每次 resolve 重新按时钟计算；状态陈旧、负缓存、回源重填、提交成功但失效失败由 Adapter 声明一致性模型。缓存测试只约束声明该能力的外部实现，不作为无缓存 Repository 的最低门槛。本轮不新增缓存示例实现或 Redis 集成平台。

docs.title: 8. CodeGenerator 与组合适配器
docs.text:
CodeGenerator:generate(ctx,input) 直接返回最终 Code。仅 code==nil 才调用它；显式空串、错误类型返回 INVALID，不能悄悄自动生成。未提供 Code 且未注入生成器返回 INVALID。显式有效 Code 可在没有生成器时创建。

生成器收到独立输入快照；它的修改不得影响实体、调用者或 Hook。最终结果必须是非空字符串；不能自动 tostring/tonumber。冲突交由 Repository，Core 不重试，也不把确定性 Hash 当作幂等创建协议。

组合参考 Adapter 接收 generator 与 encoders 有序数组。构造时校验并捕获数组顺序；拒绝洞和非编码器条目。执行时先 generator:generate(ctx)，再逐项 encoder:encode(value)；首个失败立即停止，原样返回错误。空数组合法，要求 Generator 自己返回 Code。

中间表示由相邻组件约定，Core 不建立 ID 类型联合或数值范围。Sequential/Base62 的 [0,2^53-1] 与耗尽行为保持适配器专属；完整 uint64 不能通过 tonumber 暗中进入当前 Base62。64 位字符串编码器留给有真实需求的外部实现。

docs.title: 9. Hooks 与完整用例边界
docs.text:
采用 HookPoint 的 BEFORE/AFTER、八个操作专属点及 ON_ERROR。内部 handlers[point] 是有序函数数组，没有 next()、Middleware、异步调度器或插件发现。

固定阶段顺序：通用 BEFORE → 专属 BEFORE → 操作 → 专属 AFTER → 通用 AFTER。同一运行点内按注册顺序；不能宣称不同运行点之间也按全局注册时间排序。

BEFORE 放在容器/身份等调用契约检查及输入捕获后、生成器/实体业务校验/Repository 之前，覆盖整个有效用例。每个正常返回路径恰好触发一次专属 AFTER 和一次通用 AFTER，包括 INVALID、CONFLICT 与基础设施错误。

注册点 回调签名 BEFORE_CREATE fn(ctx,point,input) BEFORE_RESOLVE / BEFORE_DELETE fn(ctx,point,identity) BEFORE_UPDATE fn(ctx,point,identity,patch) AFTER_CREATE / AFTER_UPDATE fn(ctx,point,link,err) AFTER_RESOLVE fn(ctx,point,result,err) AFTER_DELETE fn(ctx,point,ok,err) ON_ERROR fn(ctx,failed_point,hook_err)

通用 BEFORE/AFTER 收到具体操作点及相同参数。ON_ERROR 是明确的异常通知特例，第二位是失败点，不再额外传 ON_ERROR 常量。ON_ERROR 自身失败不递归。

每个回调执行前分别复制领域参数，保留 Identity/ShortLink/Resolution 的公开行为与 nil 参数位置；ctx 不复制且按只读约定使用。返回值忽略，异常逐个 pcall 隔离。未注册该点时直接返回，不构造快照。

AFTER_DELETE 的结果仍是 bool，不额外新增实体查询或返回值结构。Hook 是同步观察者，延迟计入操作，不承诺超时、沙箱、可靠投递或事务事件。

保留 issue 要求的 interactor:use(hook)：hook 是以 HookPoint 值为键、函数为值的表；统一登记到 Hooks:on(point,fn)。它与直接注册共用一个分发器，回调统一使用 v0.2 签名，不识别旧回调参数位置。

docs.title: 10. Lua 实现与性能约束
docs.text:
• 继续共享类元表、静态点号工厂、实例冒号方法，保持 Lua 5.1/5.3/LuaJIT 语法；Core 零新增运行时依赖。
  • 构造期校验 Port 方法、规则函数、编码数组和运行点，捕获配置；热路径不发现模块、不重复合并规则、不创建通用执行上下文。
  • Hooks 按点直接查数组，数字循环执行；无回调时不复制 payload。保留必要的输入、存储和观察者快照，不为节省分配取消隔离。
  • update/delete 去掉一次 Repository 预读是明确的 I/O 收益；不在本轮给出未经测量的吞吐或延迟倍数。
  • 不为行数拆分 Interactor，也不为 Pipeline 新建框架。新增内部辅助文件须有共享逻辑和可测契约的实际依据。

docs.title: 11. 迁移与验证计划
docs.text:
阶段 交付物 独立验收 A 契约冻结 评审本提案及 R1–R5，形成 RFC-0002 与 issue 的差异逐项决定 B Domain Errors/Lifecycle/ShortLink/Resolution 纯规则、等值过期、自定义规则硬约束、独立快照 C Repository 原子校验、can_update、删除规则 直接 Adapter 调用、拒绝无写入、可控交错 D 生成组合 CodeGenerator Port 与组合 Adapter 显式 Code、零/多编码器、失败短路、精度边界 E Hooks 与 Interactor 新入口与分发 四操作、无更新删除预读、正常失败 AFTER、nil 缺口 F 公共导出与打包 init、rockspec、.versions、迁移说明 安装后独立目录 CRUD；版本来源 check/sync 可用 G 文档与 CI RFC/API/双语 README/示例/合规指南/AGENTS 对齐 三解释器、逐文件95%、严格文档构建

新测试先失败再实现。保留现有成功、拒绝、快照、元组 NUL、终态和错误传播断言；仅因契约明确改变而迁移预期，不删除难测分支以满足覆盖率。

必须新增：部分规则覆盖及不改输入表；DISABLED 自定义可解析；DELETED 硬保护；相等时间过期；未知补丁和非法清除值；字段无效时不调用策略；can_update 拒绝/异常原子性；删除转换或目标状态有效性拒绝；空 Code 不生成；生成器输入隔离与 nil,nil；Pipeline 顺序/数组洞/中断；Hook 阶段顺序、正常失败 AFTER、ON_ERROR 非递归；入口捕获身份与补丁；update/delete 不 get。

测试范围继续是全部 src/ 与 adapters/ Lua 文件，每文件至少95%，包含未加载文件。Lua 5.1、Lua 5.3、LuaJIT 分别测量；Lua5.5可作额外本地检查。Codecov project/patch 至少95%、零容差。顺序测试、可控交错与真实数据库并发分别报告；外部缓存/CAS 未运行就标为未验证。

文档实施时新增 RFC-0002 与迁移说明；RFC-0001 保留为 v0.1 历史规范并标明版本。README 最短示例只使用内置 Adapter，不能以未提供的 Postgres/CachedRepository 作为开箱示例。AGENTS 中原有三个 Port、严格小于过期，以及旧文档中的 metadata 补丁忽略行为已经同步为 v0.2。

.versions 当前只匹配 init.lua 的 _M.VERSION 独立赋值及 API 文档版本行。若照附件把版本改写成表内 VERSION 字段，必须同步清单正则；否则发布脚本会失去版本来源。验收包含仓库外路径的版本 check/sync 及同步幂等，不只检查版本字符串表面正确。

验收完成后按 issue 要求，在独立 codex/ 分支提交 Draft PR；附迁移说明和实际 CI/Codecov 证据，不直接合并 main。交付检查在独立分支执行这些操作。

docs.text:
编号 差异 本轮决定 R1 issue 要求清除 expires_at，最新补充暂不提供哨兵 遵循最新补充：不新增清除功能；明确延期，不声称完成该项 R2 issue 使用 core.lua、Operations/Statuses 遵循附文：Interactor、Lifecycle/HookPoint，移除根扁平别名 R3 issue 保留 use(hook)，补充使用 on(point,fn) 保留 use(hook) 表便利入口，统一委托 Hooks:on 和 v0.2 回调签名 R4 条件更新拒绝与并发冲突 can_update=false 返回 INVALID；外部 CAS 冲突返回 CONFLICT，不新增 Core 版本字段 R5 三个公共 Lifecycle 谓词与共享归一化 新增内部函数模块 internal/lifecycle.lua，不增加公共管理器
