docs.title: 13. 实施与验证证据
docs.text:
v0.1 基线：209 项测试，15 个生产文件行覆盖率 100%。v0.2 初次全套验证：Lua 5.1、5.3、LuaJIT、Lua 5.5 各 253 项测试通过，17 个生产文件逐文件 100%；后续新增验证以 验证记录 为准。

Domain/Repository、Hooks、CodeGenerator、Interactor 均先记录失败测试再实现。独立审查检查全部生产模块，发现并修复 Repository Port 的旧错误码注释；没有据此声称验证外部数据库并发、CAS 或缓存集成。

OpenSpec 保存在被 Git 忽略的 openspec/ 中；当前设计和实施计划进入版本控制，不能将本地 OpenSpec 声称为远端已跟踪文件。保留用户原始 docs/report.md，按 issue 要求通过独立分支与 Draft PR 整体评审。

docs.title: RFC-0001: SLDS v0.1 — Short Link Domain Specification
docs.text:
Historical document: v0.2 uses RFC-0002, including Interactor, two Core ports, new Hook signatures and expiration at equality. This file preserves the earlier contract for migration review.

Field Value Status Historical v0.1 specification; superseded by RFC-0002 Version 0.1.0 Created 2026-10-08 Language Lua 5.1 / 5.3 / LuaJIT

docs.title: 1. Abstract
docs.text:
SLDS (Short Link Domain Specification) defines the identity, lifecycle, and resolution semantics of short links, while remaining independent of transport, storage, caching, security policy, observability, analytics, and deployment.

Compressed definition:

SLDS = Short Link Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics

SLDS is a pure Lua domain library — analogous to how dkjson is a JSON codec or lua-MessagePack is a MessagePack codec. It does not concern itself with HTTP routing, database access, Redis caching, or OpenResty integration. Those are Infrastructure Adapter concerns, layered on top of SLDS.

docs.title: 2. Iron Rules
docs.text:
These ten rules are the soul of the project. They MUST be placed at the very front of any implementation.

Rule Statement RULE-001 SLDS Core MUST NOT depend on HTTP. RULE-002 SLDS Core MUST NOT depend on a specific database. RULE-003 SLDS Core MUST NOT fetch Target URLs. RULE-004 Code MUST be immutable after creation. RULE-005 Code uniqueness MUST be enforced atomically by the persistence layer. RULE-006 Deleted Codes MUST NOT be reused by default. RULE-007 Resolve MUST NOT require an external event/analytics system to succeed. RULE-008 Analytics MUST NOT be part of the resolution critical path. RULE-009 Authorization MUST be implemented outside the Core Domain. RULE-010 Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass the applicable Conformance Test Suite.

docs.title: 3.1 Identity
docs.text:
The Identity answers the question: "Who is this short link?"

Identity = { namespace, code }
  • namespace — logical partition (e.g., "default", "marketing", "internal")
  • code — the short code string (e.g., "a8Kx2")

Identity is NOT: URL, Host, Domain, Tenant, User, Campaign, Database ID, or Redis Key. It is the minimal tuple that uniquely identifies a short link within the domain.

Identity is a value object — logically immutable after creation. Its Lua reference representation is an ordinary table: callers MUST NOT rewrite its fields, and operations MUST NOT mutate the caller object. Update APIs prohibit persistent identity changes; direct-assignment errors are not promised. Two Identity objects with the same namespace/code are equal.

docs.title: 3.2 ShortLink
docs.text:
The ShortLink answers the question: "What does this Identity currently represent?"

ShortLink = { namespace, code, target, status, expires_at }
  • target — the destination URL string
  • status — lifecycle status (see §3.3)
  • expires_at — optional Unix timestamp; if set and expires_at < now, the link is considered expired

docs.title: 3.3 Lifecycle
docs.text:
The Lifecycle defines three persistent statuses:

Status Resolvable? Description ACTIVE Yes Normal operational state DISABLED No Temporarily disabled (can be re-enabled) DELETED No Permanently removed (cannot be restored)

EXPIRED is NOT a persistent status. It is derived at resolution time:

if expires_at and expires_at < clock:now() then
    status = "EXPIRED"  -- derived, not stored
end

State transitions:

         create
           │
           ▼
       ┌────────┐  update  ┌──────────┐
       │ ACTIVE │ ───────► │ DISABLED │
       └────────┘          └──────────┘
           │                     │
           │     update          │ update
           └──────► (back) ──────┘
           │
           │ delete
           ▼
       ┌─────────┐
       │ DELETED  │  (terminal — no transitions out)
       └─────────┘

docs.title: 3.4 Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution is the most important capability of SLDS. It is a first-class domain operation, not an alias for Repository.get().

slds:resolve(ctx, identity) -> ResolutionResult

Resolution logic:

identity → Repository.get()
  │
  ├─ Not Found ────────────────► ResolutionResult{ found = false }
  │
  ├─ status = DELETED ────────► ResolutionResult{ found = true, status = DELETED } → not resolvable
  │
  ├─ status = DISABLED ───────► ResolutionResult{ found = true, status = DISABLED } → not resolvable
  │
  ├─ expires_at < now ─────────► ResolutionResult{ found = true, status = EXPIRED } → not resolvable
  │
  └─ status = ACTIVE, not expired ─► ResolutionResult{ found = true, target = ..., status = ACTIVE }

Key principle: Resolution is Read/Resolve Semantics, not Persistence Semantics. The domain decides whether a link can be resolved — the repository merely retrieves the data.

docs.title: 3.5 ResolutionResult
docs.text:
The ResolutionResult is the output of resolution. It does not expose the internal ShortLink entity.

ResolutionResult = {
    found      = boolean,   -- was the identity found in the repository?
    namespace  = string,
    code       = string,
    target     = string|nil, -- present only if resolvable
    status     = string,     -- ACTIVE | DISABLED | DELETED | EXPIRED | NOT_FOUND
    expires_at = number|nil,
}

Why not return ShortLink directly? Returning the raw entity would leak persistence details. ResolutionResult is a stable contract that can survive entity schema changes.

docs.title: 4. Operations
docs.text:
SLDS defines four lifecycle operations (not infrastructure CRUD):

Operation Signature Description create slds:create(ctx, input) -> ShortLink, err Create a new ShortLink Identity and Target resolve slds:resolve(ctx, identity) -> ResolutionResult or nil, err Resolve an Identity; propagate infrastructure failures update slds:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> ShortLink, err Modify mutable domain properties (target, status, expires_at) delete slds:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err Make an Identity permanently unresolvable

docs.title: 4.1 Create
docs.text:
Input:

{
    namespace = "default",       -- optional, defaults to "default"
    code = "a8Kx2",             -- optional; if omitted, Generator+Encoder produce one
    target = "https://...",      -- required
    expires_at = 1760000000,    -- optional
    metadata = {},              -- optional; Core MUST NOT interpret
}

Behavior:

  1. If code is provided (custom code), use it directly.
  2. If code is omitted, call Generator:generate(ctx) to get an internal ID, then Encoder:encode(id) to produce a short code.
  3. Call Repository:create(ctx, link) — uniqueness is enforced atomically by the repository.
  4. Return the created ShortLink.

docs.title: 4.2 Update
docs.text:
Patch fields — only mutable properties:

{
    target = "https://new-url.com",   -- optional
    status = "DISABLED",             -- optional
    expires_at = 1760000000,         -- optional
}

Code and namespace are immutable — updating them MUST fail with a programming error.

Only supplied non-nil target/status/expires_at fields are committed. Repository MUST atomically validate against the latest record and preserve unspecified fields; a DELETED record at commit rejects updates with nil,DELETED. Different-field changes survive and same-field changes follow commit order; application-level read-modify-write conflict detection is not promised. Failed validation MUST leave storage unchanged. A Service pre-read is insufficient to establish these guarantees.

Metadata patches are unsupported and ignored, preserving existing metadata contents. A nil expires_at patch means unchanged; this version defines no expiration-clearing sentinel. Expiration MUST be a finite number when present; equality with now remains unexpired.

docs.title: 4.3 Delete
docs.text:
Logical deletion — sets status to DELETED. The record may remain in the repository for audit purposes, but resolution MUST return "not resolvable" for deleted links.

Per RULE-006, deleted codes MUST NOT be reused by default.

docs.title: 5. Ports (Boundary Contracts)
docs.text: Ports are interface contracts, not implementations. SLDS Core depends on the interfaces; Infrastructure Adapters provide the implementations.

docs.title: 5.1 Repository Port
docs.text:
repository:create(ctx, link) -> link, err      -- create a new short link
repository:get(ctx, identity) -> link, err     -- retrieve by identity
repository:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> link, err  -- apply patch
repository:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err      -- logical delete

SLDS does not care whether the repository is MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, SQLite, or MongoDB. The repository implementation MUST enforce code uniqueness atomically (RULE-005).

docs.title: 5.2 Generator Port
docs.text:
generator:generate(ctx) -> id, err    -- generate an internal unique value

The generator produces an internal unique identifier (e.g., a sequential number, UUID, or snowflake ID). This is not the short code — the Encoder transforms it into a short code.

docs.title: 5.3 Encoder Port
docs.text:
encoder:encode(id) -> code    -- convert internal value to short code

The host MUST select a Generator/Encoder pair with compatible ID representations. Generic ports MUST NOT impose the reference adapters' numeric limit, alphabet or code length.

The encoder is a pure transformation — it does not need ctx (no I/O, no side effects). Examples: Base62 encoding, Base64 encoding, hash-based encoding.

docs.title: 6. Hooks (Extension Mechanism)
docs.text:
Hooks are the extension mechanism for observability — they are NOT part of the SLDS core domain.

slds:use(hook)

A hook is a Lua table with optional callbacks:

{
    before_create = function(ctx, input) end,
    after_create  = function(ctx, link) end,
    before_resolve = function(ctx, identity) end,
    after_resolve  = function(ctx, result) end,
    before_update = function(ctx, identity, patch) end,
    after_update  = function(ctx, link) end,
    before_delete = function(ctx, identity) end,
    after_delete  = function(ctx) end,
    on_error      = function(ctx, err) end,
}

Logger, Metrics, Tracer, and Audit are implementations of hooks, not SLDS core. SLDS provides the injection points; the application layer provides the behavior.

Key principle (RULE-007, RULE-008): Core MUST NOT require external analytics success. Hooks are synchronous observers: exceptions are isolated, but callback time adds latency. Each callback receives independent domain data snapshots; ctx is passed unchanged and MUST be treated as read-only. Mutations to domain payloads MUST NOT affect the operation, other callbacks or stored data. This is not an execution sandbox or durable event channel.

docs.title: 7. Context
docs.text:
ctx is just an API/Port parameter — it is NOT a SLDS domain concept.

It does not belong to: - Identity - ShortLink - Lifecycle - Resolution

It is not a core concept in the SLDS specification. At most, it is mentioned in the Ports/API Contract section:

ctx is a context table passed downward through a single SLDS operation execution. It may carry tenant IDs, trace spans, auth context, or other application-level data. The Repository implementation MAY use it for tenant-aware queries.

docs.title: 8. Architecture Boundary
docs.text:
Application / System
HTTP / OpenResty ──► Host → Namespace
                    Auth / Tenant / Policy
                    Rate Limit / Security
                    Cache / Metrics / Logging
                                   │
                                   │ Identity
                                   ▼
                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                    │            SLDS              │
                    │  Identity → ShortLink →      │
                    │  Lifecycle → Resolution →    │
                    │  ResolutionResult            │
                    │  Operations: CREATE/RESOLVE/ │
                    │  UPDATE/DELETE               │
                    │  Hooks / Ports               │
                    └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                     Repository  Generator  Encoder
                                   │
                     Infrastructure

docs.title: What Belongs to SLDS Core
docs.text: Identity, Namespace, Code, Target, Lifecycle, Expiration semantics, Resolution, ResolutionResult, Create, Update, Delete, Repository Port, Generator Port, Encoder Port, Hooks.

docs.title: What Does NOT Belong to SLDS Core
docs.text: HTTP, OpenResty, Nginx, Host/Domain, Tenant, User, Authentication, Authorization, Rate Limit, Redis, Cache, SHM, Database, Message Queue, Analytics, Click Tracking, Logger, Metrics, Tracing, Audit, URL Security, Abuse Prevention, Deployment.

docs.title: Boundary Test
docs.text: "If we remove this capability, does SLDS's Identity/Lifecycle/Resolution semantics still hold? If yes, it probably shouldn't be in Core."

docs.title: 9. Core Dependency Constraints
docs.text:
SLDS Core MUST NOT depend on:

❌ ngx
❌ ngx.req
❌ ngx.redirect
❌ ngx.header
❌ resty.redis
❌ resty.mysql
❌ lapis
❌ cjson

SLDS Core MAY use:

✅ Pure Lua (string, table, math, os, etc.)

Infrastructure Adapters (outside Core) MAY use:

OpenResty / Redis / MySQL / etc.

This constraint elevates the project from "yet another short link system" to a portable domain contract.

docs.title: 10.1 Target Validation
docs.text:
SLDS Core SHOULD validate target URL scheme at creation time:

❌ javascript:   -- MUST reject
❌ data:         -- MUST reject
❌ file:         -- MUST reject

docs.title: 10.2 SSRF Prevention
docs.text:
SLDS Core MUST NOT fetch target URLs:

❌ Do not HEAD target
❌ Do not GET target
❌ Do not validate whether target exists

Fetching the target would introduce SSRF risk into the core.

docs.title: 10.3 Open Redirect
docs.text:
Short links are inherently Open Redirects. This is a product-layer concern, not a Core bug.

Enterprise environments MAY inject a TargetPolicy:

policy:validate(target)

Allow-list example:

*.company.com
github.com
example.com

docs.title: 11. Metadata
docs.text:
SLDS Core v0.1 preserves an optional metadata = {} field on ShortLink.

Core MUST NOT interpret metadata.

metadata = {
    campaign = "black-friday",
    owner = "marketing",
    source = "internal"
}

Metadata MUST be nil or a table. Core copies raw nested table graphs at construction/export/storage boundaries, preserving cycles and shared table relationships within each snapshot and omitting metadata metatables without invoking them. Non-table leaves retain their values; mutable internals of host resources are outside this guarantee. Changes to table snapshots MUST NOT bypass Repository writes. No business schema or deep merge is defined.

Core stores and retrieves. It MUST NOT expose:

❌ link.campaign    -- business field, not domain
❌ link.owner       -- business field, not domain

docs.title: 12. Performance Targets
docs.text:
Operation Target Condition Resolve P99 < 5ms Excluding network, Core pure-memory Resolve (cache hit) P99 < 2ms Redis or local cache hit

These targets assume the Core domain logic itself is trivially fast (microseconds). The bottleneck is always I/O, which is outside Core.

docs.title: 13. Recommended Project Structure
docs.text:
lua-slds/
├── src/slds/
│   ├── init.lua                -- Module entry, public API
│   ├── domain/
│   │   ├── identity.lua        -- Identity value object
│   │   ├── short_link.lua      -- ShortLink domain entity
│   │   ├── lifecycle.lua       -- Status + transitions
│   │   ├── resolution.lua      -- ResolutionResult + resolve logic
│   │   └── errors.lua           -- Error codes
│   ├── ports/
│   │   ├── repository.lua      -- Repository port interface
│   │   ├── generator.lua       -- Generator port interface
│   │   └── encoder.lua         -- Encoder port interface
│   ├── service.lua             -- Application Service (create/resolve/update/delete)
│   └── hooks.lua               -- Hook registration mechanism
├── adapters/
│   └── inmemory/
│       └── repository.lua      -- In-memory Repository (for dev/test)
├── spec/                        -- BDD tests
├── test/                        -- E2E / benchmark tests
├── docs/                        -- Documentation
├── openspec/                    -- Specification management
└── .github/workflows/           -- CI/CD

docs.title: 14. Conformance Test Suite
docs.text:
See Conformance Test Specification for the full L0–L3 test matrix.

Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass the applicable Conformance Test Suite (RULE-010).

docs.title: RFC-0002: SLDS v0.2 — Public API and authoritative writes
docs.text:
Field Value Status Implemented in the v0.2 source branch; release/CI evidence tracked separately Version 0.2.0 Date 2026-10-18 Supersedes RFC-0001 for the current API and behavioral contracts Runtime Pure Lua 5.1 / Lua 5.3 / LuaJIT

MUST, MUST NOT and SHOULD below describe conformance requirements. API reference gives exact signatures; migration notes list breaking changes. The v0.1 RFC remains historical.

docs.title: 1. Position and iron rules
docs.text:
SLDS = Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics. Core remains a small pure Lua library; the host explicitly assembles dependencies. It MUST NOT introduce an HTTP server, database/cache client, JSON library, target request, scheduler, authorization system or durable event framework.

Rule Requirement RULE-001 Core MUST NOT depend on HTTP. RULE-002 Core MUST NOT depend on a specific database. RULE-003 Core MUST NOT fetch Target URLs. RULE-004 Identity namespace/code MUST remain immutable after creation. RULE-005 Repository MUST enforce identity uniqueness atomically. RULE-006 Deleted identities MUST remain reserved by default. RULE-007 Resolution MUST NOT require an external event/analytics system to succeed. RULE-008 Analytics delivery MUST remain outside the resolution critical path. RULE-009 Authorization MUST be implemented by the host. RULE-010 Compatibility claims MUST pass applicable conformance scenarios and declare evidence scope.

Hooks are synchronous observation points. Exception isolation satisfies no latency or telemetry delivery guarantee; the host owns any bounded/asynchronous delivery path needed by RULE-008.

docs.title: 2. API and dependency boundary
docs.text:
Core exposes only four operations through Interactor: create, resolve, update and delete. Root exports VERSION, new, Interactor, Identity, ShortLink, Lifecycle, Resolution, Errors, Hooks and HookPoint. It MUST NOT expose redundant flat status/error aliases or the former Service.

Core's dependency ports are Repository and optional CodeGenerator. Generator/Encoder remain adapter-internal components; numeric ranges, alphabets and ID representations MUST NOT constrain the generic Core port. No port inheritance or dependency container is required. ctx is an opaque table passed unchanged; it is not a dependency locator or authorization mechanism.

Constructors MUST validate injected method/function shapes. Missing Lifecycle predicates MUST be filled using defaults without modifying the host's table. The host MUST configure consistent Lifecycle functions at Interactor and authoritative Repository boundaries.

docs.title: 3. Identity, entity and rules
docs.text:
Identity is the {namespace,code} tuple of non-empty strings. It is logically immutable, represented by an ordinary Lua table with shared class metatable. Callers MUST NOT rewrite identity fields. Storage MUST preserve distinct valid tuples, including NUL-containing strings; a delimiter display string is not sufficient as a storage key.

ShortLink stores identity, target, status, optional expires_at and opaque metadata. Target MUST be a non-empty string and MUST reject javascript:, data: and file: schemes after whitespace/case normalization. Core does not fetch or fully parse the target; host policy may be stricter. Expiration MUST be nil or a finite number. Metadata MUST be nil or a table.

Only ACTIVE, DISABLED and DELETED may be persisted. Lifecycle exposes is_valid, can_transition and is_resolvable. Defaults permit ACTIVE↔DISABLED and ACTIVE/DISABLED→DELETED. Same-status patches do not invoke the transition predicate. Partial overrides may restrict states/transitions or customize resolvability, but MUST NOT admit unknown statuses, revive DELETED or resolve DELETED. Invalid business values/transitions return INVALID.

ShortLink.new(data,rules?) and with_patch(patch,rules?) perform domain validation. The allowed patch fields are target/status/expires_at. Namespace/code patches are programming errors; all other keys, including metadata, return INVALID. Nil expiration means unchanged. v0.2 defines no expiration-clearing sentinel; false is INVALID.

Metadata table graphs MUST be independently captured at construction, patch, export, storage and observer boundaries. Preserve graph cycles/shared children/table keys; omit metadata metatables without invoking them. Non-table leaves retain their values; host resource internal state is outside the snapshot guarantee. Adapters may declare a narrower serializable value set and MUST validate it.

docs.title: 4. Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution MUST be a pure domain decision and MUST NOT write Repository. It evaluates:

  1. No record: found=false, resolvable=false, status=NOT_FOUND.
  2. DELETED: found=true, resolvable=false, status=DELETED.
  3. Lifecycle denies resolution: found=true, resolvable=false, actual persistent status.
  4. expires_at <= now: found=true, resolvable=false, status=EXPIRED.
  5. Otherwise: found=true, resolvable=true, actual persistent status and target.

EXPIRED belongs to Resolution.EXPIRED and MUST NOT be persisted. The result includes namespace/code, found, resolvable, status, optional target and expires_at. Target MUST be absent when not resolvable. If custom rules allow DISABLED, a successful result MUST retain DISABLED. Hosts SHOULD decide behavior from resolvable rather than status comparisons.

Repository NOT_FOUND becomes a normal absence result. Infrastructure errors MUST remain distinct nil,err. The injected clock MUST return a finite number.

docs.title: 5. Errors and programming contracts
docs.text:
The stable error set is exactly NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT and INVALID. Expected failures return nil,err; successful values return value,nil. Delete success is true. Infrastructure errors MUST pass unchanged, without prefixes or broad exception conversion.

Missing argument containers, invalid injected methods, identity mutation attempts, malformed port responses and thrown unexpected failures are programming errors. Nil,nil from a dependency and simultaneous result/error are programming errors. A programming exception MAY propagate without AFTER; normal success and failure returns MUST trigger AFTER.

docs.title: 6. Code generation
docs.text:
CodeGenerator.generate(ctx,input) MUST return final non-empty string Code or nil,err. Only input.code==nil invokes it. Explicit invalid/empty Code returns INVALID; missing Code without a generator returns INVALID. Create fixes status to ACTIVE and rejects explicit status. The generator MUST receive independent input and unchanged ctx. Core MUST NOT coerce IDs, retry conflicts or interpret deterministic generation as idempotency.

The reference Composed adapter calls inner generator.generate(ctx), then each encoder.encode(previous) in a captured dense array. Empty arrays are allowed. Intermediate representations remain opaque; only nil signals failure. It MUST stop at first failure, preserve its error, reject malformed response pairs, and validate only the final non-empty string. This does not introduce a Core pipeline framework.

Sequential/Base62 retain exact integer range [0,2^53-1]; Sequential uniqueness is instance-local and exhaustion persists after returning the maximum once. These limits belong to reference adapter contracts. Full uint64/string IDs need separately compatible components.

docs.title: 7. Authoritative Repository
docs.text:
Repository implements create/get/update/delete. Success entities MUST be independent of storage. Create MUST reserve identity atomically, including existing DELETED records. Missing get/update/delete returns NOT_FOUND. Get retrieves an entity without applying Resolution.

Interactor.update/delete MUST NOT pre-read. Repository.update MUST atomically locate the latest record, reject DELETED, validate the complete candidate using the raw sparse patch, evaluate optional can_update, then commit. Invalid fields MUST be rejected before policy evaluation. Unspecified fields MUST remain intact; failure MUST leave storage unchanged.

can_update(current,patch) is an adapter-injected pure synchronous non-yielding boolean predicate, not a Core port. False returns INVALID. Exception or non-boolean return is a programming error with rollback. Its observations MUST NOT alias actual committed data. It MUST NOT run for delete.

Delete MUST validate the complete candidate and current→DELETED transition, including custom is_valid(DELETED). Repeat deletion returns INVALID and MUST NOT erase the identity reservation.

Different-field sparse updates preserve each other; same-field updates follow commit order. This does not promise application stale-read detection. External adapters MAY implement host-specific ctx CAS conditions and return CONFLICT; v0.2 adds no generic version fields. Cache decorators MAY implement the same port, with declared consistency and separate tests. Neither external CAS nor caching is bundled or proven by reference tests.

docs.title: 8. Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks stores ordered callback arrays by HookPoint: BEFORE/AFTER, operation-specific before/after points and ON_ERROR. Order MUST be general BEFORE → specific BEFORE → operation → specific AFTER → general AFTER, with registration order within a point.

BEFORE follows programming argument checks and snapshot capture, preceding generation/business validation. Every normal return MUST reach the corresponding specific/general AFTER exactly once. Callbacks use (ctx,point,payload...); AFTER includes value,err and AFTER_DELETE includes ok,err. ON_ERROR uses (ctx,failed_point,hook_err) and MUST NOT recurse on its own failure.

Each callback MUST receive independent domain payload snapshots preserving root domain methods and nil argument positions. ctx MUST retain its original reference and SHOULD be read-only. Callback returns are ignored; each callback exception is isolated with pcall. No timeout, sandbox, asynchronous scheduling or durable delivery is promised. Empty points SHOULD avoid snapshot allocation.

hooks:on(point,fn) registers callbacks. Interactor:use(hook) maps HookPoint values to those same v0.2 callbacks; it MUST NOT create a separate legacy dispatcher.

docs.title: 9. Verification and delivery
docs.text:
All production Lua files under src/ and adapters/ MUST individually reach at least 95% line coverage, including unloaded files, port stubs and internal helpers. Fresh LuaCov measurements MUST run separately on Lua 5.1, Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT. Codecov project/patch targets remain at least 95%, with zero tolerance. Aggregate or merged coverage cannot replace per-file gates.

Reference conformance MUST use actual bundled adapters with fresh fixture factories. Fault injection MAY replace specific methods. Deterministic interleavings MUST NOT be advertised as external concurrency proof, ctx propagation as tenant isolation, or uncached visibility as cache invalidation. Exact interpreter/test/file results and remote status belong in validation records.

Issue #6 is delivered through an independent branch and Draft PR, without merging main. The latest supplemental design defers its earlier expiration-clearing goal; this difference is explicit in migration notes. Local ignored OpenSpec proposals/specs are not part of the Git delivery unless repository policy changes.

docs.title: Reuse the suites
docs.text:
Register the four reusable suites from a Busted spec file. Replace Repository with the actual adapter being evaluated; keep fresh independent fixture state:

local Interactor = require("slds.interactor")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository")
local Composed = require("slds.adapters.composed.code_generator")
local Generator = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator")
local Encoder = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder")

local function make_fixture(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    local repo = opts.repository or Repository.new({
        lifecycle = opts.lifecycle, can_update = opts.can_update,
    })
    local gen = opts.generator or Generator.new()
    local enc = opts.encoder or Encoder.new()
    local code_generator = opts.code_generator
    if code_generator == nil then
        code_generator = Composed.new({ generator = gen, encoders = { enc } })
    end
    local clock = opts.clock
    if clock == nil then clock = function() return 1000000 end end
    local interactor = Interactor.new({
        repository = repo, code_generator = code_generator,
        lifecycle = opts.lifecycle, clock = clock, hooks = opts.hooks,
    })
    return interactor, repo, code_generator, enc, gen
end

require("spec.conformance.suites.l0_core")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l1_lifecycle")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l2_reliability")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l3_extensions")(make_fixture)

Run from a source checkout with its spec modules on package.path and installed adapter modules available. Each call creates fresh state unless a test explicitly supplies a shared Repository. Keep overrides for fault injection. The third return is now the final CodeGenerator, not the internal Generator.

L2 controlled interleavings wrap the public update method; supply a writable Lua wrapper if your adapter uses userdata. Actual external tests must isolate and clean up records while retaining required identity reservations. The fixture must configure consistent Lifecycle functions at Interactor and Repository.
